{
  "skills": [
    {
      "skill_id": "bulk_ring_lipophilicity_transfer_inverted",
      "rules": [
        "long_skeleton_hydrophobic_surface",
        "short_polar_core_penalty",
        "ring_token_scaffold_transfer",
        "large_carbon_rich_synergy"
      ],
      "ridge": 1.0,
      "prior_scale": 0.35,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.45,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.15,
      "ucb_weight": 0.6,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.2,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.01,
      "confidence": 0.6,
      "hypothesis": "Transfers ESOL size and ring roles with inverted sign, since solubility and lipophilicity are inversely coupled. Fails if length bins are chemically heterogeneous, or if pool variance is driven by polarity rather than molecular bulk."
    },
    {
      "skill_id": "halogen_aromatic_partition_vs_heteroatom_polarity",
      "rules": [
        "halogen_hydrophobic_substitution",
        "aromatic_pi_surface",
        "heteroatom_polarity_counter_prior",
        "polar_unhalogenated_hydrophilic_sink"
      ],
      "ridge": 3.0,
      "prior_scale": 0.5,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.6,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.25,
      "ucb_weight": 0.35,
      "gp_beta_start": 1.6,
      "gp_beta_end": 0.8,
      "gp_xi": 0.03,
      "confidence": 0.7,
      "hypothesis": "Transfers classical partition mechanisms: halogen and aromatic surface raise lipophilicity, polar heteroatoms lower it, while downweighting the weak donor-to-heteroatom source role. Fails if ionizable groups dominate measured logD or normalization compresses halogen effects."
    }
  ],
  "selected_skill_id": "halogen_aromatic_partition_vs_heteroatom_polarity",
  "lesson": "Cross-endpoint transfer from ESOL is directionally informative only after inversion, and its confidences are low (0.16-0.41 on 512 observations of a different property). Direct logP mechanism is the safer prior. The pool's bin distribution also matters: smiles_length_bin is badly skewed (2265 long vs 93 short), so length discriminates little, whereas halogen_high (98) and hetero_low (194) isolate sharp, chemically coherent subsets worth spending finite budget on.",
  "revision_summary": "No measured development feedback was supplied, so this revision only re-examined the earlier proposals against the original transfer evidence. Two changes were made. The ESOL-transfer skill keeps its inverted size-and-ring hypothesis but is now the lower-confidence option, flagged as fragile because smiles_length_bin is skewed (2265 long vs 93 short) and can carry little discriminative signal. The mechanistic partition skill is favored instead, and its counter-hypothesis is made explicit: the weakest source role (hbond_donor_bin to hetero_atom_bin, confidence 0.159) is reversed to a negative polarity term rather than trusted. Halogen and aromatic rules are retained for their higher transfer weights (0.7579 ring, 0.5736 length) and positive Hansch pi direction. Selection is frozen on the mechanistic skill for its sharper coverage of small, chemically coherent subsets."
}
